title.value: MaskEval: Weighted MLM-Based Evaluation for Text Summarization and Simplification
title.justification: The title directly references the introduction of 'MaskEval,' which is evaluated for 'Text Summarization and Simplification,' aligning with the main focus of the paper.
title.quote: MaskEval: Weighted MLM-Based Evaluation for Text Summarization and Simplification

extractions.description: The paper introduces MaskEval, a reference-less metric for evaluating text summarization and simplification. It utilizes masked language modeling on the concatenation of candidate and source texts and includes an attention-like weighting mechanism. This allows it to adaptively evaluate different quality dimensions such as relevance and fluency. The effectiveness of MaskEval is demonstrated on English language tasks, with the paper exploring transfer scenarios between summarization and simplification.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper is primarily focused on linguistic and computational aspects related to text summarization and simplification and does not centrally address Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development themes.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: In this work, we propose MaskEval, an adaptable reference-less LM-based metric which draws on the strengths of both approaches above. Like prior LM-based approaches, it can exploit in-domain data for fine-tuning.

primary_category.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on developing a metric for text summarization and simplification without any direct connection to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
primary_category.quote: A promising alternative is reference-less metrics which score a candidate text given only the source text.

secondary_categories.justification: No secondary themes related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development are evident in the paper's focus on computational linguistics.
secondary_categories.quote: We have proposed MaskEval, a metric for summarization and simplification that scores words in source and candidate texts using a MLM.
